transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-10
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Acme CTO), Marcus Lee (Acme SRE), Olivia Chen (Acme ML)
body:
[00:00] Lena: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Just to confirm names - I'm Lena Park, AE at Redwood, and Diego is our SE.
[00:08] Diego: hey all, Diego Ramos here - I'll cover the technical bits.
[00:12] Priya: Hi, Priya Shah, CTO at Acme Systems. Marcus and Olivia are with me.
[00:18] Marcus: morning, thanks for doing this.
[00:20] Olivia: Hi.
[00:22] Lena: Quick agenda — understand your current infra with OpenAI, drivers for migration, constraints (security, latency, cost), and see whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated or Private fits. We'll also talk about eval parity and runtime compatibility with vLLM/TGI. Does that sound good?
[00:34] Priya: Yep that's perfect. We're on a tight timeline, hoping to have something by end of Q1, ideally a pilot in December if possible.
[00:40] Lena: Great. Can you give a brief on current setup and pain points?
[00:45] Olivia: Sure. Right now we call OpenAI via their hosted endpoints for chat and embeddings. Production traffic is about 10 qps with spikes to 25. Latency is ok but cost is rising. We also run internal evals and have a bunch of Prompts that matter for accuracy.
[01:02] Marcus: We also run some inference on vLLM in-house for fine-tuned models — primarily for batch workloads — but we want predictable throughput for real-time features.
[01:12] Diego: When you say vLLM in-house, are you running TGI or HuggingFace runtimes?
[01:17] Olivia: Mostly vLLM with some TGI experiments. There's a bit of mismatch in behavior between OpenAI responses and our vLLM runs — ordering, tokenization, sometimes sampling differences.
[01:30] Lena: That's pretty common. One of the core questions we'll try to answer is eval parity: can we match the response quality and determinism you see on OpenAI when you shift to Redwood Dedicated (or Private)?
[01:40] Priya: Exactly. We want to avoid regression in customer-facing prompts.
[01:44] Marcus: Also need to confirm we can keep data in our VPC, integrate with KMS, and have audit logs for compliance. SOC two is a requirement for procurement.
[01:54] Diego: Yep, Redwood Dedicated supports private networking (VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud), and we integrate with customer KMS — we can share the exact diagram.
[02:03] Priya: Great — would you be able to support HSM or only cloud KMS?
[02:08] Diego: We support cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and customers can route to an HSM-backed key if that's available via their KMS. We also emit audit logs.
[02:19] Olivia: On the model side, what's the workflow for bringing our prompts and comparing responses?
[02:24] Lena: Typical pilot: you give us a representative eval set and a sample of production calls. We run parity checks across the candidate models — Redwood-provided and any BYO models — and compare metrics you care about: accuracy, hallucination rate, latency, cost per token.
[02:38] Olivia: OK. How do you handle runtime differences vs vLLM/TGI? We've seen tokenization and sampling nuances cause differences even when the model checkpoint is the same.
[02:48] Diego: Good point. Our runtime does kernel and compilation-level optimizations; sometimes that changes numerical properties. We try to surface exact model config (temp, top_p, sampling seed if requested) and we can run deterministic sampling for evaluation. But there are edge cases — we log and, if necessary, we can match vLLM's behavior by adjusting decoding (e.g., using greedy or deterministic seeds) or by running on a fallback runtime that more closely mirrors vLLM/TGI.
[03:12] Priya: Does Redwood host the same weights as OpenAI or are these open models?
[03:17] Lena: For many models we host open-source weights (Llama variants, Mistral, etc.), not OpenAI proprietary weights. If you rely on OpenAI proprietary endpoints, we can help evaluate comparable open checkpoints or keep a hybrid approach — you can route high-value calls to OpenAI while moving most traffic to Redwood Dedicated.
[03:35] Marcus: We need to know about request routing and fallback — in case Dedicated is saturated can we route to Hosted or another region?
[03:43] Diego: Yes, we have smart routing policies — can route by latency, cost, or SLO. There are fallback policies to hosted or alternate model variants. We can also do canary and A/B rollouts.
[03:55] Priya: What about metrics and observability? We need token-level cost breakdowns per route and tracing to link calls back to our logs.
[04:04] Diego: Redwood Console gives per-route/model dashboards, token breakdowns, and tracing hooks. We also support exporting traces to your Observability stack.
[04:11] Lena: Quick question on your security posture — is SSO/SAML required?
[04:15] Priya: Yes, SSO and RBAC for the console. Also we'd like to see penetration test reports and SOC2.
[04:23] Diego: We'll attach our SOC2 report and our pen test summary. SSO via SAML/Okta supported; RBAC is configurable.
[04:30] Olivia: For the eval parity run — how long does a bench take and what are the compute costs?
[04:35] Diego: For a representative eval set (say 10k prompts) we can run in a day; costs depend on model size and concurrency. For Dedicated we provide a pricing worksheet that estimates GPU-hours. We'll include a sample cost breakdown.
[04:50] Priya: Can you speak to quantization/accuracy tradeoffs? We've tried 4-bit quant on vLLM and saw small accuracy hits.
[04:58] Diego: We recommend specific quantization profiles per workload; Redwood Optimize will suggest profiles. For mission-critical prompts we run higher-precision or keep a fallback to full precision models. We'll call out expected delta in eval metrics.
[05:12] Marcus: Any chances of tokenization differences causing production errors?
[05:16] Olivia: yeah, like token offsets in embeddings.
[05:18] Diego: We try to standardize tokenizers; if you have a custom tokenizer we can run tests. For embeddings, we validate alignment and can do a migration checklist.
[05:28] Lena: Turning to procurement — what's your timeline and success criteria?
[05:32] Priya: Timeline is Q1 roll out, pilot in December. Success criteria: parity on top 200 prompts within 3% of current accuracy, average p95 latency under 350ms, predictable monthly cost under our threshold.
[05:44] Lena: Makes sense. We'll include these in the pilot proposal. Any blockers?
[05:48] Marcus: Procurement will need SOC2 and legal review. Data residency is also a question for some EU users but most of our traffic is in US.
[05:56] Diego: We have region controls and can isolate capacity per region.
[06:00] Priya: One more thing — if we start with Dedicated, and later want on-prem or VPC-only, is that supported?
[06:06] Lena: Yes — Redwood Private is our option for VPC/on-prem. The control plane model differs, but config and API surface stay consistent.
[06:13] Olivia: Are there any gotchas when moving from OpenAI to your hosted open models? We tried to mirror prompts and saw some hallucination regressions.
[06:22] Diego: Hallucination delta can be model-specific. We'll run targeted evals and tune temperature/top_p, or recommend different model checkpoints, and provide a fallback policy to OpenAI for critical calls during the pilot.
[06:36] Priya: Sounds reasonable.
[06:38] Lena: Ok let's recap next steps: Lena sends pricing/sizing, Diego sends security packet and integration guides, Olivia provides eval prompts and sample data, and we'll schedule the technical deep dive for the week of Nov 17.
[06:53] Marcus: That works.
[06:55] Priya: Thanks — also please include a simple migration checklist for embeddings and for chat.
[07:02] Diego: We'll include a checklist and a short runbook.
[07:06] Olivia: One last quick Q — do you have any references or customers who migrated from OpenAI to Dedicated?
[07:11] Lena: Yes — we can share two references and a short case study. I'll include contact info in the follow-up.
[07:17] Priya: perfect.
[07:18] Lena: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by Wednesday with the materials.
[07:22] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[07:24] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: Automatic transcript, occasional mis-IDs (e.g., "Redwood dedicate" for Redwood Dedicated), some filler words removed.
